label: copy-phase z input late in long sequences, esp. when next output is r/z/f/p
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely (97% of mass) when the fed-back input is z (rarely r). Never fires in the original phase or on the delimiter, and never at recall_idx < 3. It fires on only about 5% of copy-phase z inputs, and those are concentrated at late absolute steps (t >= 12, i.e. long sequences with L = 8-9). It is strongest when the token being output after z is r (out_tok r: 53% of mass, and the top examples are almost all z followed by r), then z, f or p. Short sequences with z followed by r stay inactive. Recall-oriented: copy z & t>=12 covers 89% of mass at 7% precision. The out_tok restriction raises precision to about 40% while keeping 76% of mass. The remaining selectivity is not captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+5.83), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+4.92), in_tok=z (+3.88), phase=2 & out_tok=r (+3.21), out_tok=r (+3.07), prev_tok=h (+2.69). Lower it: recall_idx=2 (-3.03), prev2_tok=<DEL> (-3.03), recall_idx=1 (-2.68), prev_tok=<DEL> (-2.68).
